Whoff Agents Research and development
Eidolon
Realistic decoy phone activity around one protected phone, built so the pattern an outside observer can see stops pointing at one person.
In development
Request a pilot conversation
See what it does
What it is
A small carry-along device plus an operator console.
Where it stands
In development. The device hardware is in design and nothing has shipped.
Illustrative model, not measured traffic or performance.
The signal
Encryption hides the content. It does not hide the pattern.
A phone going about its day gives an outside observer plenty to read, without opening a single message.

Lock Put together, the pattern points at one person.
The crowd
Now give that phone a crowd.
Eidolon surrounds the protected phone with realistic decoy phone activity. Each decoy keeps a daily rhythm of its own. It is built so the pattern stops pointing at one person, while that person stays connected.

One stream, many lanes
Following one identity shows only a fraction.
Proven in the lab
The protected phone's traffic fans out across the decoys' lanes. An observer who follows any one identity sees a fraction of the stream. Splitting works in the lab. It has not run on a device yet.

Illustrative model, not measured traffic or performance.
One stream It leaves the phone as a single flow.
Many lanes It fans out across the decoys' lanes.
A fraction Any one lane carries only part of it.
They keep up with you
Move, and every decoy re-plans in its own time.
The decoy behavior engine re-plans on the spot from where the device actually is. Each decoy changes what it is doing at a different moment, so they never move in step.

Each decoy in its own time. They never move in step.
A full day, no link
Plan at the dock. Then 24 hours dark.
24-hour plans run on a test phone
The operator console plans a window and assigns the decoys. Undocked, the phone agent carries the plan on its own, with no link to the operator. Docked again, the console produces the report.

One day, start to finish
Plan at the dock
Undock
24 hours dark
Dock again
Read the report
The phone agent has run full 24-hour plans on a test phone at the bench. It took no instructions once a run started, and it stayed cabled for power and measurement. The console runs today against simulated devices and one test phone. The device hardware is in design.
Where it stands
What runs today, and what does not yet.
Eidolon is in development. This is each part as it stands, in plain terms.
Current maturity
Protection effectiveness has not been established. The scenes on this page are an illustrative model, not measured traffic or performance.
Status board
In development
Decoy behavior engine
Runs today
Each decoy keeps its own daily rhythm (commuter, shift worker, traveler, resident) and re-plans on the spot from where the device actually is: place, motion and time of day.
Phone agent
Run on a test phone
It has run full 24-hour plans on a test phone at the bench, taking no instructions once a run started.
Operator console
Runs in test
It plans a window, assigns decoys and produces a report afterwards. It runs today against simulated devices and one test phone.
Traffic splitting
Proven in the lab
Splitting a protected phone's traffic across several decoy lanes works in the lab. It has not run on a device.
Detector challenge
Before any claim
Decoys are challenged with our own detectors before any protection claim is made.
Device hardware
In design
The device hardware is in design. Nothing has shipped.

Ask for a pilot conversation.

Organizations only.
United States only for now.
Requests are reviewed before any reply.
Eidolon is in development, and nothing here is a performance guarantee.

Where it stands
Request
(described as) Illustration. One phone's activity resolves into a clear pattern of where, when and how much, and a reticle locks onto the phone.
(described as) Illustration. Decoy phones appear around the protected phone, each with its own daily rhythm, and the reticle moves between them without settling on one.
(described as) Illustration. The phone's single stream of traffic fans out across several decoy lanes. An observer following one lane sees a fraction of the stream.
(described as) Illustration. A device moves from home to work to a store. After each change, each decoy changes what it is doing at a different moment.
(described as) Illustration. A plan is loaded at the dock, the device undocks and runs for 24 hours with no link, then docks again and the operator console shows a report.
(described as) On this page
